steps.path: Contribute to YouCoded, and the bug and feature ticket screens
steps.headline: This is what done means for the two Development screens you approved.

rows.statement: The walkthrough of how contributing works lives inside Contribute to YouCoded, not on the Development list.
The walkthrough explains contributing in plain words: describe it, review the design, try it, run checks, then choose to propose it.
Nothing becomes a public proposal until you approve it at the last step of the walkthrough.
The walkthrough has no gray warning box under its five steps.
rows.note: just delete the wierd warning in the gray box. what is "workspace details"? "set up separate workspace"? why not jsut "set up development workspace"?

rows.statement: Contribute to YouCoded leads with one sentence about its purpose and one setup action.
The setup action is a full-width main button like the app's other dialogs, with no caption beneath it.
The same full-width button sits under the five walkthrough steps.
The Contribute screen matches the app's other settings pages: short text, clear headings, evenly sized buttons.
rows.note: this is also just ugly, too much text, poor visual heirarchy, weirdly sized buttons. doesn't match our other settings pages.

rows.statement: Setup leaves an existing development folder untouched and explains that the new project is separate.
rows.threshold: an existing folder is unchanged after setup runs in a dev instance

rows.statement: You can start working in the new project on this device even when its backup has not connected.
rows.threshold: setup finishes and the project opens with backup unavailable

rows.statement: A ticket starts with the error and app version; recent logs are only included when you choose them.
You can write, review and send a ticket without any AI help; asking an assistant is a separate choice.
You prepare and review a ticket in YouCoded, then finish attaching approved screenshots or files in GitHub.
Before you attach a file, the screen says GitHub uploads it immediately, before you submit the ticket.
The ticket screen opens with an editable title and description, a public-sharing notice, and optional error details.
Both the bug tab and the feature tab sit under one heading: Submit a ticket.
Optional AI help appears only on the review step, behind a disclosure you open yourself.
The ticket's optional evidence sits in three plain rows under one heading, each explained by the (i) on its row.
The ticket screens use the same compact rows as other settings menus, without dense blocks of text.
rows.note: there's way too much poorly organized copy with unclear visual heirarchy. we need to simplify this and make it better match existing settings menus.

rows.statement: Review ticket is a full-width main button that stays inactive until you have typed a title and description.
No preview or mockup captions appear anywhere; Submit is the main button with Back to draft beneath it.
Error details shows your real app version rather than a line saying nothing was collected.
If sending a ticket fails, your title, description and chosen details stay in the draft and you can retry.
